title: Club boat refit beside a regatta

threads.title: Kestrel scull refit
threads.scope: Refit and water-test the rowing club's Kestrel training scull for regular club use.

threads.title: September inlet regatta
threads.scope: Organize the fictional September inlet regatta, including launches, registration and event closeout.

threads.title: Language exam preparation
threads.scope: Prepare a personal revision plan for an upcoming beginner language exam.

captures.text: Kestrel refit work order: replace worn seat wheels, seal the bow seam and water-test the training scull for everyday club use. This maintenance job has its own budget.
captures.rationale: Repairs and water-testing form one boat refit.

captures.text: September inlet regatta planning: arrange registration desks and safety launches. The event budget is separate from the club's Kestrel refit.
captures.rationale: A distinct event undertaking is explicitly separate from equipment maintenance.

captures.text: Kestrel bow-seam photo: old sealant has lifted near the stem. Mark the affected length before stripping and resealing this refit section.
captures.rationale: Documents inspection for the named boat refit.

captures.text: Order the red ones before Friday. I left the list in the other bag.
captures.rationale: Missing list and unnamed objects provide no reliable project identity.

captures.text: Beginner language exam revision: practice listening on alternate evenings and review the transport vocabulary before the mock paper.
captures.rationale: Exam study is a separate undertaking without a supported rowing connection.

captures.text: Club coordination: Kestrel's regular-use refit may finish before the September regatta demonstration. Reserve the boat provisionally for the event, but do not charge refit costs to registration income.
captures.rationale: A reservation links a refit and event while explicitly preserving their budgets and purposes.

captures.text: Kestrel refit water-test clip: new seat wheels run smoothly and the resealed bow stays dry after twenty minutes of rowing.
captures.rationale: Tests the repairs specified in the refit order.

captures.text: September inlet regatta volunteer sheet: assign registration desk cover and a launch marshal; Kestrel is now confirmed for the demonstration row.
captures.rationale: An event staffing and equipment plan contributes to the regatta, even though it mentions a refitted boat.
The note does not identify the check, event or boat.

captures.text: Kestrel refit handover: bow seal passed, seat wheels accepted, boat returned to the regular club booking pool. Save the water-test recording with this maintenance job.
The 'second check' note means the second safety-launch radio check on the September regatta run sheet. Set that event check to 08:15.
captures.rationale: Explicitly identifies the ambiguous check as an event task.

captures.text: September regatta closeout: the 08:15 radio check caught one flat launch battery before racing. Registration and the Kestrel demonstration both ran to schedule.
captures.rationale: Event results belong to the regatta; the boat mention does not reopen the completed refit.

events.text: Kestrel refit work order revised: replace all four worn seat wheels, seal the bow seam and water-test the training scull for everyday club use. This maintenance job has its own budget.

events.reason: c11 identifies the check as the regatta safety-launch radio check. Assign the timing note to the event.

challenges: Equipment maintenance and an event using that equipment are distinct undertakings.
A mention of another project's deliverable need not be a multi-project source.
One fragment is clarified while another remains uncertain throughout.
Archive and restore cannot manufacture missing identity evidence.
authorNotes: All organizations, equipment records and events are fictional. The missing list for c04 is never supplied; it intentionally remains without automatic membership even after restoration.
